what_it_does: Energy-harvesting systems (EHSs) are tiny computers powered solely by harvested energy — from radio waves, solar cells, or vibration — with no battery, so they shut off whenever the ambient energy dips. Modern processors try to speed things up by prefetching: guessing which memory blocks a program will need soon and loading them into fast on-chip memory (cache) ahead of time. On a battery-powered device this is usually worthwhile, but on an EHS, prefetched data that sits in cache when the power cuts out is simply lost, and the energy spent fetching it was wasted. IPEX is a lightweight add-on that wraps around any existing prefetcher and teaches it to be conservative on EHSs: it tracks which prefetched blocks were actually used before the last power failure and stops prefetching lines that historically go unused. It also watches the harvested energy level and, when a power cut looks imminent, dials back prefetching so the remaining energy goes toward useful forward progress instead.
